title: The Void Has a Sense of Humor
logline: When a crying, phone-clutching kid runs from the Void, Jesus strolls up and whispers it a joke; the Void laughs up galaxies, wants a word, gets refused and blocked, and walks off giggling into the sunset; and, in a bonus memory, the same Void quietly mule-kicks a Depression Magician into the buckets so it can have a moment with my fear.

voice_notes.NARRATOR: The storyteller, the 'I', spinning a daydream out loud for one friend and half cracking up at it. Same gender-neutral voice as the earlier film, but present tense and playful: 'let's say' is a magic wand (and the empty-path pause after 'Jesus appears...' is a held magic trick). Warm, wry, quick, with a laugh always one breath away (on 'like, on their ass', 'Maniacally', the block, 'too intensely', 'Bonus scene') and never mocking anybody. 'I have theories.' is the driest line in the film. Drops into a conspiratorial hush for whispers, side-eyes and the magician's entrance. Plain and tender, never preachy, on the true lines: 'it hears that a lot', 'Not yet. But maybe.', 'It wants you to stop feeling anything at all.', and the last lines of the bonus. The final 'Tee-hee.' is soft, delighted and a little moved.
voice_notes.JESUS: Warm, unhurried, playful, utterly unafraid; the voice of someone who smiles while he talks. A gentle tease, never preachy. His comedy is his sincerity: 'The void's got a pretty good sense of humor' is a cozy recommendation; 'Tee-hee' is a real little giggle; his 'mm-hm's under the Void's whisper sound like a phone call with a friend; 'No, I know. That hurts.' is suddenly quiet and real; 'I'll ask.' has a faint 'oh, this is going to be a whole thing' under it; 'Oh, boy' comes out through clenched teeth. To the user he goes quiet, low and level, every word placed ('You were crying before it ever showed up, you know.' offered like a blanket); 'Fair.' is a breathy chuckle at their sass; then the enthusiasm bursts out on 'more about emotions!' and 'meaningful to me!': brighter, faster, too much, too soon. 'Too much eye contact. Apparently.' is bone-dry; the neutron joke is told with a tiny silly voice for the neutron, a gruff one for the bartender, and visible pride in how bad it is.
voice_notes.USER: Young, quick, gender-ambiguous-to-feminine, the voice scraped thin from crying. Fear comes out as sarcasm: fast, flat, clipped. 'Uh. Sir? That's the void.' is squeaky, half-whisper, half-shout. 'What the actual f***?!' cracks high, half sob, half shout. 'Hell no' is flat and absolute; 'scary thing' wobbles and gives them away. 'Wasn't planning on it.' is brittle. 'I just...' is the only unguarded thing they say, and it cracks. 'Nope.' and 'Way too much eye contact.' are a door shutting.
voice_notes.FEAR: Small, breathy, high, quick to crack; the same Fear as the earlier film. 'What's... what's that noise?' is a worried little stammer with a gulp; 'Oh. ...Okay.' is small and trusting; 'Why are you showing me this?' is barely a whisper, awe not fear, exactly as in the first film.
voice_notes.MAGICIAN: A theatrical, slithery stage-magician voice in a stage whisper: wet consonants, savoring every word, a giddy creepy giggle underneath. Comic menace, never truly frightening. '...Rude.' is muffled from under a bucket, small and dazed.
voice_notes.VOID: Never speaks words. All vocals are non-verbal and musical: a snort and a giggle that leak out before a huge booming laugh that collapses into wheezes and squeaky giggles; airy starry whispers we can never understand (one of them slower and sadder than the rest); kettle-like huffs that puff out nebulae; a long soft sigh; a bubbly, surprisingly high giggle; a snort that sprays stars; an innocent rising 'hm?'; a low warm hum, like a cat purring in a cathedral. Its face does the talking.

scenes.purpose: A bright, inviting first frame that sells the whole premise in one glance: a crying kid with a phone fleeing a huge, soft, starry presence across a pastel dream at golden hour. We laugh a little, worry a little, and notice two things the kid can't: the Void isn't hunting anyone (it's trying to say 'wait'), and the crying started on the phone, before the Void was ever in the picture.

music.mood: comic-anxious scurry over a warm dusk
music.instrumentation: pizzicato strings, light marimba, a soft low clarinet on each of the Void's footfalls, warm string pad underneath; the scurry thins for one bar under the phone insert

beats.shot: OPENING STILL / THUMBNAIL. Frame 0 is the finished, fully lit image: no fade from black, nothing fading up. 35mm-feel lens, camera at chest height, tracking backward down the pale winding path at running speed. Left of centre: the USER running straight at camera, framed knees-up, face at y≈540, mid-sob. Right of centre, on the crest of the peach hill behind them: the VOID, huge and round, hood top at y≈255, starlight eyes at y≈360, body down to y≈800, violet-to-teal rim glow against the gold. Above the Void hangs its own private pocket of indigo starry sky; the title 'The Void Has a Sense of Humor' sits in that clear indigo sky in soft cream rounded lettering at y≈110-230, centred, fully opaque, never overlapping the hood (cream on indigo, high contrast). Around them: lilac and mint hills, a rose-gold crystal tree at left, the enormous low warm sun far down the path at right, three or four glowing thought-seeds drifting in the light. Warm sun rim on both characters; the phone throws a cool white glow on the user's chin. Below y≈850 only pale path and mint grass. The title holds through this beat and fades out over the first 1.5 s of the next.
beats.action: The user runs toward us, crying, phone clutched to their chest; behind them the Void plods after them on short fat legs, one big hand half-raised, the other lifting its hem a little like a long skirt so its fat legs can waddle. A thought-seed drifts across the top third.

acting.USER: In pose on frame 0, eyes open (never mid-blink), never a smear: right foot planted, left arm pumping, right hand clutching the phone to the sternum. Eyes huge and wet, pupils small, lower lids shoved up by the sob, inner brows yanked up and together, mouth a wide open sob-square, a tear streak catching gold on each cheek; cowlick bouncing; glasses slightly askew. At 1.0 s a look back over the left shoulder (the eyes lead, the head follows 3 frames later), a sharp gasp-breath, and the eyes snap forward even wider.
acting.VOID: Not menacing, and the frame should say so: eyes big and round, lids high, brow-wisps tilted up in the middle (worried, hopeful), mouth a small soft 'o'. Its right hand is half-raised out of the sleeve, four fingers spread, the gesture of someone calling 'wait, hang on'; the left pinches the hem up off its round fat feet. Each step sets its whole round body jiggling like a water balloon; a star mote lifts off one shoulder.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: So, let's say there's a Twitter user...
beats.delivery: warm and conspiratorial, a smile in the voice, like starting a daydream out loud for one friend; a tiny breath after 'So,'; a little lift on the last two words, as if picturing them
beats.shot: Continue the backward track while the title finishes fading out; drift a touch closer so the user fills more of the middle (face y≈480). On 'user', a 1.0 s insert over the user's thumb: the phone screen fills the upper-middle (y≈300-800), a generic social app with a plain white speech-bubble icon (no logo, no real names), grey posts with little storm-cloud icons sliding up under the thumb.
beats.action: The user keeps running at us, and even now their eyes drop to the phone. In the insert, a tear falls onto the glass and blooms into a small blur over a grey post, and the thumb scrolls straight through it. (They were crying at this before anything was chasing them.)

acting.USER: Runs, sobbing in rhythm with the stride, a hitched breath every second step. Mid-run the eyes drop to the phone (habit, even now): the thumb flicks the feed up twice, smears the tear, keeps scrolling; a tiny tremor in the hand. Then the eyes jerk back up.
acting.VOID: Plods behind, hand still half-raised, eyes fixed hopefully on the user's back.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: crying, and running from the ~void.
beats.delivery: a little slower, mock-solemn on 'running from the void' (the low note does the drama for us), a suppressed laugh caught in the breath at the end
beats.shot: Cut to a wide from low on the path ahead, 24mm feel: the USER small in the lower-middle (head y≈600) sprinting toward camera; the VOID rising behind them all the way up to y≈170, its full round bulk and hood against its indigo sky-pocket, gold sky on both sides. Its sheer size fills the frame behind the tiny running kid.
beats.action: On 'crying', a sob visibly shakes the user's shoulders; on 'running from the void', the Void keeps pace behind them with surprisingly quick, short, round shuffle-steps under its lifted hem.

acting.USER: On 'crying', the chin crumples, the eyes squeeze to wet slits, and two little tears fly off sideways as glints. On 'void', a frantic look back: the eyes lock onto the Void for 6 frames, pupils pin, the mouth stretches into a silent scream-grimace, teeth showing. Arms start to pinwheel; running is clearly not their sport; one sneaker scuffs.
acting.VOID: When the user looks back, the Void's eyes brighten and its raised hand gives a tiny hopeful wave, two finger-wiggles. The user's face contorts; the hand freezes mid-wiggle, and the brow-wisps sink at the outer ends. It keeps following anyway, small puffs of star-breath motes from its mouth with each step.

scenes.purpose: Jesus arrives on the storyteller's cue (after a beat of nothing at all), and in one look he understands everything: the terror, the tears, and the Void, whom he seems to recognize. He is not afraid, and the camera knows it. The Void, for its part, is not used to anyone walking toward it.

music.mood: the chase stops dead for the cue; then a warm, light surprise
music.instrumentation: the pizzicato chase cuts out for the empty-path pause (only wind and approaching footsteps); on 'Now' a harp glissando and a celesta glint; warm strings; the chase falls away to a few plucks

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: And let's say Jesus appears...
beats.delivery: setting up a magic trick: breezy and a little grand; the voice hangs in the air on 'appears' and waits, and waits
beats.shot: Cut to a locked-off medium of an EMPTY bend in the path beside a rounded rose-gold crystal tree, the low sun behind it. The centre of frame (y≈300-800) is open and empty. Hold on the emptiness through the whole pause; nothing gathers, nothing glows.
beats.action: Nothing appears. That is the joke. The empty path just waits in the golden light; one thought-seed floats down into frame, bobs once, and drifts off. Off-screen, the user's running feet and wet, gasping breath get closer and closer.

acting.USER: Off-screen, heard only: running feet and ragged sobbing breath approaching from frame left.
acting.JESUS: Not there. Not yet.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: ^Now.
beats.delivery: a crisp little stage cue, a snap of the fingers in the voice, landing exactly on the sparkle
beats.shot: Same locked-off frame.
beats.action: On 'Now', JESUS is simply there in the middle of the path with a soft golden shimmer and a small puff of warm sparkles (no flash, no halo disc), already mid-evening-stroll, as if he'd been walking this path for an hour. Face at y≈330-430.

acting.JESUS: Appears mid-step and relaxed: hands loosely clasped behind his back, head tilted up toward the sky, eyes half-lidded in plain contentment, an easy closed-mouth smile. A slow breath of pleasant evening air lifts his chest. One slow, satisfied blink. He has not noticed anything yet.

beats.speaker: USER
beats.shot: Cut to a slightly low medium two-shot from the side: JESUS standing calmly at frame right (face y≈380), the USER bursting into frame from the left, still looking back over their shoulder (face y≈420).
beats.action: The user whips their head forward, finds a whole person suddenly standing right there, and screams.

acting.USER: Head snaps forward; eyes fly wide, pupils pinpoints; brows shoot up; mouth a tall open oval; the body jolts upright mid-stride, arms flung up; the phone pops out of the hand and is caught again.
acting.JESUS: A small surprised blink at the scream; the brows lift; he does not step back. A tiny polite tilt of the head: oh. Hello.

beats.shot: Hold the two-shot; the camera dips to follow the user down (their face settles at y≈620, well above the subtitle band).
beats.action: The user skids, their legs shoot out in front, and they land hard on their backside, sliding to a stop right at Jesus's sandals in a puff of pale dust. They twist round to face the Void lumbering up behind them, scoot backward twice on heels and one hand until their back bumps Jesus's shins, and throw the other hand up, palm out, toward the Void.

acting.USER: The skid: eyes wide, mouth an 'O', arms windmill, and the phone is held up high to save it (priorities). THUD on the backside: the whole face compresses on impact and the glasses jump. A frantic twist round toward the Void; scoot, scoot, bump (the back meets Jesus's shins; they don't even notice). The left hand shoots up, palm out, fingers splayed, at the Void; the right clutches the phone to the chest. Eyes enormous, pupils tiny, lower lids trembling, upper lids sky-high; shoulders up at the ears.
acting.JESUS: Looks down at the kid now leaning against his shins: brows lift in sympathy, inner corners up; a soft 'oh' shape of the mouth; his hands come out from behind his back, open.

beats.shot: Reverse, low angle from just behind the USER's raised hand (the hand soft in the foreground at y≈700) up to the VOID, which has stopped three metres away (eyes y≈260).
beats.action: The Void stops. Its half-raised hand hovers, then slowly lowers into its sleeve; the lifted hem drops back over its feet. Then it takes one tiny step back.

acting.VOID: Stops on one foot, wobbles, settles both feet. Its eyes go to the user's raised palm: a slow blink. The brow-wisps sink at the outer ends; the upper lids drift down to 70 percent and the lower lids lift a touch: a quiet, familiar sadness. The hand lowers back into the sleeve. Then one tiny half-step backward, to give the user room.
acting.USER: In the foreground, the raised hand trembles; the breath comes in fast little gasps.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: And he sees all of this.
beats.delivery: gentle and a little fond; slower; 'all of this' with a small lift, as if gesturing at the whole mess
beats.shot: Close on JESUS, face y≈420, a slow push-in.
beats.action: We watch Jesus take in all of it with his eyes: the crying kid at his feet, the phone, the huge Void.

acting.JESUS: Eyes go down to the user on the ground and hold 12 frames: inner brows up, mouth soft; a flick to the glowing phone in their fist, hold 6. Saccade up to the Void; hold; then recognition: the outer brows lift, a small warm crinkle at the eyes, one corner of the mouth twitches up. Oh. It's you. Back to the user. On 'this', a slow blink: the thought changes. When the lids open the eyes are bright and one corner of his mouth tucks up: he has an idea. A slight nod to himself.

beats.shot: Medium wide, 35mm, camera at the seated user's eye height: the USER on the ground in the lower-left foreground (head y≈640); JESUS steps past them, heading for the VOID, who stands in the upper-middle background (eyes y≈240).
beats.action: Jesus walks past the user toward the Void, and as he passes he gives the user a small, calm, palm-down 'one sec' gesture. The Void glances behind itself.

acting.JESUS: An easy, unhurried walk. Passing the user he lowers his right palm in a gentle 'hold on, one sec', with a small reassuring smile and a nod, and does not break stride.
acting.USER: Eyes follow him (eyes lead, head follows slowly). The raised hand stays up but bends at the wrist in confusion. The mouth closes, then falls open again as it dawns on them where he is going.
acting.VOID: Sees him coming: the eyes widen, and it glances over its own shoulder, behind itself, as if he must be walking toward somebody else. Nobody there. Its eyes come back to him, round and uncertain; its hands knot together at its middle.

scenes.purpose: Fearless intimacy as comedy: the one person who walks toward the scary thing does it like greeting an old buddy. We never hear the joke; we watch it land on the Void's face in slow, precise stages, and the storyteller refuses to tell us what it was.

music.mood: playful, sly, tiptoeing
music.instrumentation: pizzicato walking bass, a low clarinet, soft vibraphone, brushed snare; everything drops to one held harp note under 'I have theories'

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: So Jesus walks right up to the void,
beats.delivery: brisk and delighted, like reporting something slightly outrageous; a light stress on 'right up'
beats.shot: Medium-wide two-shot from the side, 35mm: JESUS walks into frame left (face y≈430); the VOID towers at right (eyes y≈230); its starry sky-pocket overhead.
beats.action: Jesus walks right up to the Void and stops at its side, close enough to touch.

acting.JESUS: Arrives with a little hop on the last step and looks up at it with a big friendly smile, brows raised, the face of someone spotting a buddy across a party.
acting.VOID: Leans back slightly as he arrives: eyes wide, lids up, brow-wisps up and apart, mouth a small surprised 'o'. A star mote pops off its shoulder.

beats.speaker: USER
beats.text: Uh. Sir? That's the void.
beats.delivery: fast and squeaky, half whisper, half shout, the voice scraped thin from crying; the politeness of someone watching a stranger walk up to a bear
beats.shot: Quick cut: close on the USER on the ground (face y≈420), the two figures soft behind them.
beats.action: From the ground, the user whisper-yells a warning at Jesus.

acting.USER: Lip-synced. Leans forward on the free hand; the eyes flick between Jesus and the Void, Jesus and the Void; brows up and knotted, inner corners high; the raised hand flaps once, a feeble 'stop'; on 'void' the mouth pulls wide and tense; two quick tiny head shakes, no-no.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: puts his arm around it,
beats.delivery: rolling on, warmer, enjoying this
beats.shot: Back to the side two-shot, a little tighter: Jesus waist-up, the Void's face and middle.
beats.action: Jesus puts his arm around the Void; it is so wide that his hand only reaches the velvet curve of its side.

acting.JESUS: Lifts his right arm and drapes it around the Void as far as it will go, which is not far; settles it with a pat; looks up with a wide smile and an eyebrow bounce: hey, buddy.
acting.VOID: Freezes. Its eyes drop hard to the arm around it, slide to Jesus's face, drop to the arm again: two quick blinks. Its hands float up a few centimetres from the sleeves, not knowing what to do with themselves, then sink. Stiff as a startled cat, shoulders up around the hood.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: and starts whispering in its ear.
beats.delivery: dropping into a whisper on 'whispering', as if we're in on it now
beats.shot: Slow push to a medium two-shot of their heads: the Void bends down until its hood is level with Jesus's face (both faces y≈330-400).
beats.action: The Void bends down; Jesus rises onto his toes, cups a hand beside his mouth, and starts whispering into the side of its hood.

acting.JESUS: Up on his toes; left hand cupped beside his mouth; eyes twinkling sideways at it; brows lifting in small conspiratorial hops; lips moving close to the hood.
acting.VOID: Lowers its huge hood slowly toward him, the way a tall friend bends to hear in a loud room. The eyes slide toward him, then lose focus: listening.

beats.speaker: JESUS
beats.caption: (whispers a joke)
beats.shot: Close-up on the VOID's face (eyes y≈380), Jesus's cupped hand and bearded profile soft at frame left. A very slow push-in.
beats.action: Jesus whispers the joke. We never hear the words. It lands on the Void's face in stages.

acting.VOID: 0.0 s: listening, eyes unfocused, lids neutral, mouth closed. 0.8 s: one brow-wisp lifts at its outer end, skeptical. 1.4 s: the eyes slide toward Jesus and narrow slightly: really? 2.0 s: the lower lids push up (a smile starting behind the eyes) while the mouth stays pressed in a flat line. 2.6 s: the corners of the crescent mouth twitch, twice. 3.2 s: the eyes squeeze shut into upturned arcs.
acting.JESUS: Whispering steadily; between phrases his own lips press together to keep from laughing at his own joke; his shoulders give one tiny shake.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Nobody knows what he said. I have ^theories.
beats.delivery: dry, a perfectly straight face; the driest line in the film; a tiny pause before 'theories'
beats.shot: Pull back to the medium two-shot; the USER visible small and soft at the lower-left edge (head y≈700).
beats.action: The Void fights the laugh with everything it has: a big hand clamped over its mouth, its whole round body quivering. Not one star has escaped yet.

acting.VOID: Clamps a big hand over its mouth. Its whole round body quivers like a jelly; the eyes are squeezed into wet, shining arcs above the fingers; the stars inside its velvet fizz faster; under the hem the fat feet do a small involuntary shuffle-dance.
acting.JESUS: Drops back onto his heels, hands folded, an innocent, satisfied little smile; eyebrows up; one small nod: wait for it.
acting.USER: Staring, mouth open, phone held up in front of the face as if it could protect them; one slow, disbelieving blink.

scenes.purpose: The release, built in threes: a dead-still hold, a snort, a giggle, then an enormous, maniacal, joyful laugh that spills stars and galaxies. Funny because it's huge; touching because the Void clearly hasn't laughed like this in a very long time; terrifying, from where the user is sitting.

music.mood: a held breath, then a comic eruption into sparkle that peaks with the big galaxy
music.instrumentation: a single held harp note for the still hold; one glockenspiel ping on the snort-star, two on the giggle-stars; then a timpani roll and low brass on the burst, glockenspiel and harp glissandi on the stars, a bouncing bassoon underneath, a cymbal swell on the beach-ball galaxy

beats.shot: Close two-shot, JESUS and the VOID, heads at y≈300-460. Locked off.
beats.action: Everything stops. The Void goes perfectly still behind its hand.

acting.VOID: Absolutely still; hand over its mouth; above the fingers the eyes open, blank and round; one slow blink; then the lower lids begin to twitch upward.
acting.JESUS: Perfectly still too, eyebrows up, lips pressed together, holding in his own laugh; eyes fixed on the Void's eyes.

beats.speaker: VOID
beats.shot: Same frame.
beats.action: A snort bursts out and ONE tiny star pops out between its fingers, arcs up and twinkles away.

acting.VOID: The shoulders jolt once; the eyes squeeze into crescents; the hand presses harder over the mouth.
acting.JESUS: Grins; nods encouragingly, eyebrows high: right?

beats.speaker: VOID
beats.shot: Slight push-in.
beats.action: The giggle leaks out through its fingers and TWO more stars squeeze out between them and float up.

acting.VOID: The body bobs with each giggle; eyes watering starlight; brow-wisps fluttering up; it tries and fails to hold it in, fingers spread over its mouth.
acting.JESUS: Starts giggling silently too, shoulders shaking, a hand on his chest.

beats.speaker: VOID
beats.caption: (maniacal cosmic laughter)
beats.shot: Cut on the burst to a low-angle medium wide, camera at Jesus's chest height, 28mm: the VOID's head thrown back (eyes y≈220), JESUS beside it at frame left (face y≈470), the star sky-pocket above.
beats.action: The dam breaks: the Void bursts out laughing, head thrown back, the mouth wide open into a crescent full of stars.

acting.VOID: The hand flies off its mouth; the hood snaps back; the mouth opens into a huge crescent with deep cosmos and stars inside; eyes squeezed into tight upturned arcs; brow-wisps fly up; the whole body bounces on each 'HA'; both hands clutch its round belly.
acting.JESUS: Laughs silently along with it: shoulders shaking, eyes crinkled shut, one hand on its side.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: And then the void starts laughing. ^Maniacally.
beats.delivery: trying not to crack up; a hiccup of laughter before 'Maniacally', which is then said with delighted precision
beats.shot: Hold the low-angle wide; a gentle 5-degree orbit around them.
beats.action: The Void keeps laughing, maniacally, rocking on its fat little legs.

acting.VOID: Rocks backward and forward; one fat leg lifts and stamps; it slaps the side of its own cloak.
acting.JESUS: Laughing, wiping the corner of one eye with a knuckle.

beats.speaker: VOID
beats.shot: (continues under the narration)
beats.action: The laughter rolls on under the narration.

acting.VOID: Peal after peal, with whistling wheezes between them; tiny starry tears leak from the eye-arcs.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: So hard, it's coughing up stars...
beats.delivery: building, awed and amused at once
beats.shot: Cut to close on the VOID's face (mouth y≈430), stars visible inside the crescent.
beats.action: On 'coughing up stars', the Void coughs mid-laugh and a spray of little bright stars pops out of its mouth and floats upward, twinkling.

acting.VOID: A cough doubles it forward mid-laugh: the eyes pop open in surprise as a puff of stars bursts out of the mouth; it looks at them; it laughs even harder.

beats.speaker: VOID
beats.shot: (under the line)
beats.action: Cough, laugh, cough: stars spill out with each one.

acting.VOID: Each cough pops out another little cluster of stars.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: and little ^galaxies.
beats.delivery: a delighted little squeak of disbelief on 'galaxies'
beats.shot: Medium on both, then a quick follow-pan down as a small spiral galaxy tumbles out of the Void's mouth, bounces on the grass and rolls away downhill out of frame.
beats.action: The Void coughs up a little violet-and-gold spiral galaxy the size of a dinner plate; it bounces on the grass and rolls off down the path like a dropped coin, toward the user.

acting.VOID: One big hiccuping cough: the galaxy shoots out; the eyes go wide and cross for a beat; a big hand reaches after it, misses; then it laughs harder.
acting.JESUS: Leans back to let it pass his nose, eyes following it down the hill, a delighted 'ooh' mouth; then he's laughing again too.

beats.speaker: VOID
beats.shot: (under the line)
beats.action: One big cough-hiccup produces the galaxy.

acting.VOID: One big hiccuping cough.

beats.speaker: VOID
beats.shot: Wide, 28mm: the Void and Jesus in the upper half; the USER in the lower foreground (head y≈680); the air above them full of drifting stars, against the dusk.
beats.action: The peak: the Void rears back for one last huge howl and coughs up the biggest one yet, a spiral galaxy the size of a beach ball, which sails slowly over the user's head and hangs in the sky, turning. (It stays up there, turning, for the rest of Part One.) Jesus pats the Void's back.

acting.VOID: Rears up to full height, arms flung wide, mouth enormous, eyes clenched; on the big cough the whole body jolts and the big galaxy launches out; then it doubles over, one hand on Jesus's shoulder for support, the laugh thinning into wheezy high squeaks.
acting.JESUS: Patting its back in rhythm and laughing with his whole face, eyes closed into crescents, mouth open in a warm laugh; one glance up at the big galaxy with delighted 'ooh' brows.
acting.USER: Flattens back on the elbows as it passes over; the eyes track it all the way up; the jaw drops.

beats.speaker: JESUS
beats.shot: (under the Void's laugh)
beats.action: Jesus laughs with it.

acting.JESUS: A soft, warm, breathy laugh under the Void's.

beats.shot: Low on the path beside the USER's sneaker (the sneaker lower-right at y≈800, the user's face upper-middle at y≈400 behind it; the laughing pair small and soft up the hill).
beats.action: The little galaxy rolls into frame, spirals to a stop against the user's sneaker, wobbles like a spun coin and lies down flat, still twinkling.

acting.USER: Looks down at it. Then, very slowly, looks back up the hill. One slow blink. The raised hand has not lowered an inch. Terror and total incomprehension at once: the brows can't decide (left up, right down); jaw hanging.
acting.VOID: Background, soft: still shaking with leftover giggles, wiping one eye.

scenes.purpose: The title line lands. Jesus, still glowing from the laugh, looks at the terrified kid on the ground and tells them the Void is funny, as if that settles everything. The comedy is the canyon between his ease and their terror, and the 'tee-hee' that falls into it.
